title: Image Prompt Techniques: From Reference Photo to Generation
lede: The complete prompt-engineering field manual for fashion imagery — six-layer decomposition, palette-first reference borrowing, and the two-iteration validation loop. Written from 4,700 real outfit references.
body_md:
## The six-layer decomposition
Every great fashion prompt is six layers inside-out: subject → outfit (type+fabric+color) → pose → scene → light → medium. Skip one and you get 'roughly right, totally wrong mood'.

## Layer 2 deep-dive: the outfit sentence
Formula: garment type + fabric behavior + precise color. 'a camel wool coat over white straight-leg trousers' beats 'nice coat and pants' by an order of magnitude.

## The palette-first method
When referencing a photo or game costume: extract palette → silhouette → material trio, never copy frames. Palette borrowing is the copyright-safe creativity.

## The two-iteration loop
Translate → generate → diff against the reference → fix the weakest layer → regenerate. Two cycles is usually enough; more means your reference was ambiguous.

## Medium words that actually matter
'street style photography, 35mm, film grain' ≠ 'professional photo'. Medium words set the render engine's entire texture bias — treat them as a layer, not garnish.
faq: How long should a fashion prompt be?
40-80 words. Under 30 loses the mood layers; over 120 makes models average everything out.
